artworks.title: Dionysus, Acme, and Icarius (House of Dionysos mosaic)
artworks.description: Paphos mosaic — Dionysus bringing the first wine to Icarius, the Attic gift that will cost the host his life.

artworks.title: Dionysos and Ikarios (Farnese relief)
artworks.description: Farnese relief — the god visiting Icarius with the vine, the hospitality myth before the shepherds' murder.

artworks.title: The Sleep of Erigone
artworks.description: After Girodet — Erigone asleep before she finds her father's body and the Aiora swinging rites begin.

artworks.title: Erigone Ensnared by Dionysus
artworks.description: Print of Erigone and the vine — the daughter of Icarius caught in Dionysus' gift that named her grief among the stars.

artworks.title: Bacchus and Attendants Visiting Icarus
artworks.description: After-antique visiting scene — Bacchus at Icarius' door with the wine that Attica will learn to fear and celebrate.

popCulture.title: Icarius (Athenian)
popCulture.description: The Attic host of Dionysus who shared the first wine — murdered by shepherds, mourned by Erigone and the dog Maera, and set among the stars.

popCulture.title: Erigone (daughter of Icarius)
popCulture.description: Daughter who finds her father's body and hangs herself — the Aiora swinging rites and Virgo still remember her grief.

popCulture.title: Boötes
popCulture.description: The constellation tradition that places Icarius among the stars — wine's first teacher as the herdsman of the northern sky.
